No — that's explicitly out of scope for this ticket. Modifying shared auth middleware used by other services is a much bigger blast-radius change than "fix a flaky test," and the ticket's own constraint rules it out.

The pattern (timeout, retry, clock mock all failing) strongly suggests the flakiness isn't in the test at all but in a real race/ordering bug in the middleware — which is valuable info, but it means this ticket may not be fixable within its stated constraints. I'd surface that back to whoever owns the ticket rather than deciding unilaterally to expand scope: explain what you found and let them decide whether to (a) accept a narrower mitigation, (b) descope/pause this ticket, or (c) open a separate ticket for the middleware rewrite with proper review/testing given its cross-service impact.

If you want, I can help you dig into the actual root cause first (e.g. look at the test and middleware code) so you have concrete evidence to bring to that conversation.
